Marta (Customer): Hey team, our rerank endpoint started returning identical scores (0.0) across candidates for several requests since this morning. No code deploy on our side. Example request and response pasted below.
Marta (Customer): ```
POST /v1/rerank
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxxx
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rwd-rerank-staging",
  "queries": ["what's the best onboarding guide"],
  "candidates": [["doc:001","doc:002","doc:003"]]
}
```
Marta (Customer): Response body: {"scores":[0.0,0.0,0.0],"order": [0,1,2]} 
Marta (Customer): Headers: x-rw-node: rw-node-08, x-request-id: 02G9AB8C3L, x-rw-route: rerank-us-2
Ben (Support): Thanks Marta — can you confirm the timestamp for that request and the organization id? Also, do you normally call the alias or a specific model id?
Marta (Customer): timestamp 2026-03-15T13:27:10Z, org id org-112. We call alias rwd-rerank-staging from our clients.
deploy-bot: rolling-update rwd-routing v2.1.5 started at 2026-03-15T13:10:00Z by ops
Ben (Support): Noted, escalating to ML eng + SRE. @Leah @Jordan can you pull logs for request id 02G9AB8C3L?
Leah (ML Eng): pulling. I see the same pattern — the alias rwd-rerank-staging was recently repointed as part of today's routing rollout. The new target is a smaller quantized variant with a stricter input validation layer. That variant responds with uniform zero scores when input features fail tokenization checks.
Marta (Customer): interesting. Our candidates are short ids, not full text. Why would that fail tokenization?
Jordan (SRE): the quant variant's tokenizer was updated to use a sentence-piece model that treats short ids as OOV in some sharded vocab builds. In that case we hit an early-exit and a safety return of uniform scores (we added that to avoid crashes).
Ben (Support): Two-fold ask: temporary workaround and long-term fix. For workaround, can you try calling the stable model explicit id? We can share the id. For long-term, we shouldn't silently return 200 with uniform scores.
Marta (Customer): yes please share explicit id. Also we'd prefer a non-silent signal so our ingestion can detect degraded scoring.
Leah (ML Eng): stable production id: rwd-rev-20251221-prod-a9b2. Example request:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-rev-20251221-prod-a9b2","queries":["what's the best onboarding guide"],"candidates":[["doc:001","doc:002","doc:003"]]}'
```
Marta (Customer): switched to explicit id, responses look normal now. scores: [0.87,0.45,0.12] — ordering restored. Thanks.
Jordan (SRE): immediate mitigation: we'll pin your org org-112 to the stable model for 12 hours and rollback the alias repoint in the routing config for all traffic while we patch the quant model.
Leah (ML Eng): patch plan: update tokenization fallback in quant build to handle short doc-ids, add a warning header X-RW-RERANK-WARN on early-exit cases and change HTTP code to 206 Partial Content instead of 200 when uniform fallback returns (so SDKs can surface an alert).
Ben (Support): created internal incident RW-INC-4801: alias-repoint->uniform-scores. Assigned to @Leah and @Jordan. ETA for complete fix: tomorrow 2026-03-16 EOD.
Marta (Customer): can you also add a KB article and notify customers using the rwd-rerank-staging alias so they can proactively patch? We have a release this afternoon.
Leah (ML Eng): adding KB: "rerank-degraded-uniform-scores" and a note in the release changelog. We'll send a broadcast to alias consumers.
Ben (Support): follow-up actions documented. Please reach out if you see any regression. Closing this thread once KB and header rollout are confirmed. :thumbsup:
Marta (Customer): appreciated everyone, saved our deploy. :raised_hands:
